title: Holographic quantum codes with trapped ions
authors: Alex Steiner, Gerard Anglès Munné, Robert Freund, Ivan Pogorelov, Michael Meth, Robert J. Harris, Gavin Brennen, Thomas M. Stace, Thomas Monz, Rainer Blatt, Felix Huber, Martin Ringbauer
abstract: Holography is a central concept at the intersection of gravity, condensed matter theory, and quantum information, linking the interior bulk of a system to its boundary. A model realizing key features of holographic systems is the holographic pentagon code by Pastawski et al. Here we experimentally implement instances of the holographic pentagon and heptagon codes with trapped ions and test their properties: For the pentagon code, we recover logical bulk qubits from their nearby boundary and test the Ryu-Takayanagi entanglement area law. For the heptagon code, we show that the transversal Hadamard gate native to the constituent Steane codes induces a single-qubit, correctable error in the holographic code. Our implementation paves the way towards the use of holographic quantum codes for quantum information processing.
summary: This paper experimentally implements holographic quantum codes, specifically the pentagon and heptagon codes, on a trapped-ion quantum processor. The research tests how encoding information based on geometric principles allows for partial recovery of quantum data from boundary measurements. This work advances the field by demonstrating a physical pathway toward using gravity-inspired concepts in fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The research investigates the experimental realization and testing of holographic quantum error correcting codes to bridge concepts from gravity (holography) with practical quantum computation.
main_result: The authors successfully implemented holographic pentagon and heptagon codes using trapped ions, demonstrating partial recovery of logical information and performing basic logical gates.
method: They utilized trapped ions for physical implementation, testing code properties like partial decoding (recovering bulk qubits from boundary measurements) and measuring fidelity against theoretical predictions.
model_or_system: The system is a trapped-ion quantum processor using $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ions. The model involves encoding information into graph codes derived from holographic principles, specifically the pentagon and heptagon structures.
key_observables: Logical qubit fidelity (DFE), expectation values of stabilizer generators ($g_1$ to $g_{10}$), and successful recovery of logical bulk qubits from boundary measurements.
important_parameters: The code sizes tested include the pentagon code (4 logical qubits) and heptagon code. The physical platform uses Mølmer-Sørensen gates for entanglement.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the theoretical framework of partial recovery, which differs from traditional full decoding requirements; experimental measurements are subject to quantum projection noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the holographic structure (pentagon/heptagon), show the process of partial decoding via cuts $\gamma$, and compare measured expectation values of stabilizer generators against numerical simulations for gate operations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the theoretical concept of holographic codes to detailing the experimental implementation on trapped ions, testing specific code structures (pentagon/heptagon), and finally demonstrating logical operations and error detection capabilities.
why_interesting: This work directly connects fundamental concepts from quantum gravity (holography) into a tangible platform for quantum information processing using trapped ions, providing an experimental testbed for advanced QEC theory.
